speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In Singapore, where we pride ourselves on being efficient and attentive in all that we do, we certainly need to do more and do better in workplace safety and health, or WSH.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But COVID-19 seems to have undone all the hard work and strides that we have made.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers, who were quarantined for varying periods, returned to new worksite layouts, unfamiliar team members and constantly changing safe management measures at their worksites.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Measures meant to keep them safe from the COVID-19 virus might have unwittingly raised the risk of an accident happening.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The tripartite partners recognised this and encouraged employers to conduct Safety Time-outs four times in the past 18 months – in December 2020, February and June 2021, and most recently in May this year.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While I am sure that the numerous Safety Time-outs have helped companies to re-evaluate their WSH practices and prevented an even sharper rise in workplace fatalities, the unfortunate truth is that workplace accidents, injuries and fatalities are still occurring at an alarming rate.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Labour Movement is deeply concerned – and rightfully so.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Injuries sustained because of a workplace accident can also have lifelong debilitating effects.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The right to a safe workplace is fundamental, sacred and we must do all we can to uphold this.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While these are indeed important measures, the Government's actions alone are not enough.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Together, they make up the acronym RIGHT, R-I-G-H-T.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, we must establish safe and easy-to-use reporting channels for anyone to report unsafe workplace practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: MOM's investigations into workplace fatalities often find that unsafe, unsupervised practices had been ongoing for a period of time.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Those at the workplace would sometimes even say that is "normal practice".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In some cases, workers would tell us that the unsafe practices had been escalated to their supervisors, but nothing was done.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Tragically, the inaction can lead to someone dying from a preventable accident.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must therefore provide a better whistle-blowing channel – one that ensures the anonymity of whistle-blowers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should make near-miss reporting more prevalent in the industry, as these are early warning signs of accidents to come.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must also allow anyone, including members of public, to report unsafe workplace practices when they see them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In 2016, The New Paper reported how Mr Gusharen Singh snapped pictures of safety lapses at worksites and public spaces and alerted MOM through the Snap@MOM crowdsourcing app.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Could we consider leveraging the OneService mobile application to allow anyone to report unsafe work practices?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: After all, everyone has a part to play when it comes to safer workplaces.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Next, I hope that MOM can partner the unions to supplement their routine inspections.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Since 2019, NTUC has been training our union leaders on WSH.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, more than 1,000 union leaders have completed the courses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: MOM could consider sharing the data received from feedback channels with NTUC and our union leaders can partner MOM in stepping up safety inspections at these companies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Having union leaders will add an element of moral suasion to MOM's inspections and help convince workers and supervisors alike to pay more attention to workplace safety.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the public transport sector, the National Transport Workers' Union initiated the Rail Industry Safety and Health Community of Practice to enhance safety for our rail workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Earlier this year, the union, together with LTA and the public transport operators, launched the Safety Champions initiative to empower frontline transport workers to proactively surface feedback and areas for improvement to enhance safety at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should strive to replicate this model of tripartite collaboration in other industries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond doing one-off safety inspections, I hope that MOM will also regularly reinspect companies with poor WSH performance to ensure that sufficient safety measures have been implemented and prevent these companies from "relapsing" into poor WSH practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Third, workers should be properly geared at the workplace so that their safety is not compromised.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: NTUC LearningHub stands ready to offer training courses to all workers so that they can continually refresh their WSH knowledge.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond ensuring workers are well trained, we need also to ensure that supervisors and management are geared with the right WSH mindset.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We can train someone to be the best lifting supervisor, but if his management does not appreciate the dangers involved, his hands could be tied if critical resources are not deployed for his safety needs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In a recent interview with The Straits Times on 29 July, Minister Tan See Leng said that most workers who died at the workplace in the last few months were experienced staff and a factor driving up workplace fatalities involved employers pushing staff to catch up on the backlog of work.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This just goes to show that even the most experienced of workers can fall victim if tiredness seeps in and causes a momentary lapse in concentration.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If employers are pushing our workers to quite literally work towards their deaths, then we must surely act to stop this.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Next, buy-in from higher management is vital if we truly want WSH to be pervasive at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The culture at the top shapes practices on the ground.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In Australia, it is a legal requirement for company directors and business owners to ensure employees’ safety at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Company directors have been held liable for fatalities, such as a recent case in June 2020, where two directors of the Brisbane Auto Recycling Proprietary Limited were sentenced to jail when a worker was killed by a forklift operated by an unlicensed operator.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The bottom line is that company directors must not only be aware, but also act on their WSH roles and responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lastly, we should leverage technology, a key enabler to detect and prevent workplace accidents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, workplace safety technology has matured to a level that is possible to predict the risk of workplace accidents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, sensors and wearables can alert management when a worker deviates into a restricted area, or when a worker slips, trips, or falls, allowing medical help to be dispatched quickly.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Big data and predictive analytics provide the potential of predicting accidents before they even happen.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some companies have already started to trial body-worn cameras for their workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is something that we should pursue especially in high-risk worksites.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Body-worn cameras not only facilitates near-miss reporting and aids in post-incident investigations, but they also allow workers to be more conscious of their actions and behaviour at the worksite.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The cost of such technologies, however, can be prohibitive and it takes an enlightened management, usually large multinationals, to invest in them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should help our SMEs adopt such technologies to improve their WSH outcomes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The new centre should focus on lowering the adoption cost of new workplace safety technologies through demand aggregation and facilitate the deployment of such technologies in our SMEs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is imperative that we do so as smaller companies cannot possibly hope to emulate the strong WSH practices of large companies without proper support.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Government procurement can also lead by example and favour companies that adopt WSH technology as part of the tender bid.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is already practised in Sweden today and we should implement this in Singapore too.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Like the internal audit functions that many companies have, having a dedicated WSH representative will ensure that sufficient attention is dedicated to WSH issues, no matter how big or small.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I therefore, sincerely hope that the MOM will consider my numerous proposals on this issue: make every company have a mandatory WSH representative.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Let us do what is RIGHT and ensure that our workers can go home safely at the end of every workday.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore has reached a stage of development where we can and we should be held to higher WSH standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We made good progress to reduce workplace fatal injury rates from 2.1 per 100,000 workers in 2012, to 1.1 per 100,000 workers last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have set high workplace safety standards in Singapore because we want all our workers to return home safely to their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is not just an aspiration, but a shared mission with our tripartite partners and industry stakeholders Since the higher fatality trend surfaced in April this year, MOM has ramped up inspections, imposed stiffer penalties and conducted Safety Time-outs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In my response, I will share further measures to strengthen companies’ WSH ownership, step up inspections and enforcement, and raise awareness and promote WSH, so that more companies will want and will be equipped to do well by WSH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The inculcation of a safety culture, which underpins safe workplaces must start with the top management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Managements set the tone, the culture and they also allocate resources within their organisations, which ultimately shape WSH practices on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The law today already places WSH responsibilities on company leadership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the ACOP, corporate leaders and Boards of Directors will be guided on their WSH responsibilities, including conducting ground engagements and communicating the need to prioritise WSH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Member asked about the legislative “teeth” of ACOP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the event of a WSH Act offence, the Courts will consider the ACOP when assessing the culpability of a company, its leaders and its Board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They can and will be prosecuted if found to be culpable for safety lapses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM has completed the first round of industry consultation and will commence public consultation this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are putting Managements and Boards on notice, that the ACOP is coming.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To further strengthen management commitment, MOM will harmonise the criteria for disqualifying contractors with poor workplace safety practices from public sector’s construction contracts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also reviewing the Demerit Point System to ensure errant contractors are sufficiently penalised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This includes debarring them from employing foreign employees for a period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To provide transparency on companies’ safety records, CheckSafe on MOM’s website allows anyone, particularly developers and service buyers, to check safety track records before engaging contractors and vendors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Inspections and enforcements form a key part of MOM’s efforts to uphold WSH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We conduct targeted inspections of companies in higher risk sectors such as construction, manufacturing, transportation and storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Those with poor WSH performance are inspected more frequently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Simple and totally avoidable mistakes that resulted in loss of lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I urge companies and workers to take these safety requirements seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our inspectors also spend time to advise companies on the WSH rectifications that are needed, so that they can learn and sustain improvements over a period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I encourage union leaders to rally company management to do more walkabouts and join them too, in this effort to strengthen WSH commitment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, the MOM hotline and e-feedback are easily accessible to everyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Information on these channels is prominently displayed on signboards at construction worksites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To raise awareness among migrant workers, MOM has also shared these channels via WSH Alerts on the FWMOMCare app and through our partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On Member’s OneService app suggestion, MOM is already exploring adding the MOM e-feedback function into another whole-of-Government app – we will let you know once that is ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Anyone, including members of the public, who witnesses safety lapses or poor safety practices should not be afraid to inform their management or to report them to MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I wish to assure anyone who comes forward that there are existing safeguards to protect them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Inspectors maintain this confidentiality strictly when they follow up with the companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the WSH Act, employers cannot dismiss or threaten to dismiss workers who have reported WSH contraventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM will not hesitate to take enforcement actions against those that do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Member spoke about requiring a WSH representative in every company beyond the higher risk companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM is reviewing the coverage of the existing WSH personnel and will update the industry once we complete our review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For workplaces not already covered, we strongly encourage companies to identify employees or perhaps, even NTUC can recommend union leaders to take on these tasks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, they are required to attend training on risk management as part of the bizSAFE programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, that requirement already exists for those on the bizSAFE programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The WSH Council is already working with NTUC to develop micro-learning modules for worker refresher training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We plan to expand this to include relevant programmes for supervisors and management, so that they can lead their company’s safety culture more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I agree that it can be a contributory factor of workplace accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I would encourage the unions and workers to keep MOM informed if there are contraventions to the Employment Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I also agree with the Member that WSH technology is a key enabler to detect and prevent workplace accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are heartened to know that more companies are adopting WSH technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Members will be pleased to note that WSH technology solutions are incorporated in the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs) developed by Infocomm Media Development Authority and sector lead agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are available to firms, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have made significant progress and we must take important lessons from this episode to build a safety culture that will endure for years to come.
